recommendation.summary: S5 FD-passing process handoff with identity state transfer (new binary).
justification: dependency/toolchain/runtime/native/embedded change needs a new binary; S5 keeps the listening socket and transfers state unchanged (state schema identical)

goroutine-structure, long-running or start-up code changed: in-process patching would leave old code running in goroutines that never return; a new process starts the new goroutine structure, and the old one is drained and exits

S6 blockers (10): github.com/mattn/go-colorable: dependency graph changed; github.com/rs/zerolog: dependency graph changed; github.com/gotify/server/v2.main: main() runs once at start-up (never re-executed / never returns); github.com/gotify/server/v2/api.NewOIDC: start-up-only code already ran; its effect is baked into the live state, so patching it changes nothing; github.com/gotify/server/v2/plugin.Manager.loadPlugins: start-up-only code already ran; its effect is baked into the live state, so patching it changes nothing; ... and 5 more
alternatives: Kubernetes rolling update (loses in-memory state, needs surge capacity)
risks: changed functions are small enough to be inlined; with S6 slot trampolines the call still dispatches through the slot, but raw binary patching (internal/livepatch) must also patch the inlining callers: github.com/gotify/server/v2/api/stream.client.startReading, github.com/gotify/server/v2/api/stream.client.startWriteHandler
no patched function has a context.Context parameter: S6 gives per-call (not per-request) consistency, so one request may mix old and new versions of the 17 functions
1 patched functions are in package main; a Go plugin cannot import package main, so hotpatchgen must relocate them into an importable package
type information is partial (298/328 type errors old/new; third-party packages are opaque): call-graph and state reachability are lower bounds
quiescence: old activations of main(), init-started or long-running goroutines never return, so the old process is retired by exit, not by draining; set a drain deadline in the S5 upgrader
